Following Apple's earlier promise that Tim Cook would continue to be involved in the company's global government relations after stepping down as CEO, he met with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen this week. Here are the details.

Tim Cook discusses EU Kids Act with Commission President

When Apple announced earlier that Tim Cook would step down as CEO on September 1, the company stated:

Since taking on the role of Executive Chairman, Cook has been keeping that promise.

A few days ago, Bloomberg reported that Cook would attend the state dinner hosted at the White House on Thursday evening (September 24) for Chinese President Xi Jinping.

A few days after that report was published, Cook posted on X that he had hosted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at Apple Park.

After the meeting, Albanese reportedly revealed that Cook described Australia's social media restrictions for children as "world-leading."

Yesterday, Cook continued his series of meetings with world leaders, sitting down with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

von der Leyen posted on X that the two discussed the EU Kids Act and "agreed on the importance of privacy, safety and protection for children."

The proposed legislation would limit minors' access to social media across the entire EU and require platforms to provide stronger safeguards for young users.

The meeting took place in Manhattan, where world leaders are currently gathered for the United Nations General Assembly.

It remains unclear whether Cook will or has met with other world leaders, but if so, chances are we will hear about it soon from the relevant officials.
